PC1.label: Violation type

PC1.1.label: Incorrect policy information given
PC1.1.description: Agent stated a specific Scopus policy rule incorrectly — e.g. quoted the wrong processing timeline, wrong re-evaluation criteria, wrong coverage period, or wrong threshold.

PC1.2.label: Applicable policy not referenced
PC1.2.description: A directly relevant Scopus policy rule existed and governed this ticket's situation, but the agent did not mention, apply, or reference it in their response.

PC1.3.label: Policy misinterpreted
PC1.3.description: Agent reached broadly the correct conclusion but explained the reasoning incorrectly — e.g. cited the wrong policy rule, gave the right answer for the wrong reason, or conflated two different policy criteria.

PC1.4.label: Policy correct but explanation insufficient
PC1.4.description: Agent applied the policy correctly and the outcome was right, but the explanation given was too brief, unclear, or jargon-heavy — contributing to the customer's confusion or dissatisfaction even though no factual error was made.

PC1.5.label: Not applicable
PC1.5.description: Use when agent_response_compliance is 'compliant' or 'no_policy_applies'. No violation is present.

PC1.description: The type of policy handling error or gap identified in the agent's response.

PC2.label: Policy area

PA0.label: No applicable policy
PA0.description: The ticket topic is not governed by any Scopus content coverage policy in the reference document.

PA1.label: Title selection and CSAB evaluation
PA1.description: Covers minimum criteria for title consideration, CSAB evaluation categories, and the selection process statistics.

PA2.label: Re-evaluation and discontinuation
PA2.description: Covers the three-metric flagging system, two-year rule, RADAR tool, formal complaint triggers, and the 5-year re-consideration rule.

PA3.label: Document type coverage
PA3.description: Covers which document types are included and excluded (book reviews, meeting abstracts), and trade journal minimums. -- For the full specific exclusion list (obituaries, ads, reprints, interviews, etc.) see PA11.

PA4.label: Conference proceedings coverage
PA4.description: Covers the full-text-only rule for conference proceedings and subject area focus.

PA5.label: Processing timelines
PA5.description: Covers the 2-3 week (e-feed), 4-5 week (paper), and 4-day (AiP) processing timeline commitments. -- AiP-specific processing rules (mandatory DOI, no volume/page, no grant info) are classified under PA10, not PA5 -- For missing content reports, a minimum 6-week publication maturity threshold applies before investigation is initiated (see PA18 criterion 5).

PA6.label: Coverage period and historical content
PA6.description: Covers the year-of-selection-minus-4 rule (from 2023) and pre-1996 title handling.

PA7.label: Metrics methodology
PA7.description: Covers CiteScore calculation method, SJR, SNIP, and the annual recalculation cycle.

PA8.label: Book and book series selection
PA8.description: Covers publisher-based book selection policy and how individual book requests are handled.

PA9.label: Preprint server coverage
PA9.description: Covers which preprint servers are indexed and that preprints do not affect metrics. -- Server source IDs: arXiv 923623402, bioRxiv 923623403, ChemRxiv 923623404, medRxiv 928910002, SSRN 931193761, TechRxiv 937262106, ResearchSquare 937262107 (CAR Manual S6).

PA10.label: Article-in-Press (AiP) eligibility and processing
PA10.description: AiP items carry unit type ARTICLE-IN-PRESS and status S200. DOI is MANDATORY for all AiP items. No volume, issue, or page data required. Grant info (grantlist) NOT captured. Items appear in Scopus within 4 days of publisher FTP delivery, distinct from PA5 standard 2-3 week e-feed timeline. Violation: agent quotes 2-3 week SLA for an AiP query; agent says DOI optional.

PA11.label: Excluded item types (CAR Manual S1 list)
PA11.description: These item types are NOT indexed: book reviews; obituaries (incl. "In Memoriam"); advertisements; society news; notices of future conferences/events; reprints published elsewhere; personal reports; indexes; addendums; product/video/audio reviews; award winner notifications; interviews; Instructions to Authors; "In this issue" / TOC items. Book reviews and conference meeting abstracts also covered under PA3. Use PA11 when the customer missing item falls into one of these specific excluded categories.

PA12.label: Patent indexing and coverage
PA12.description: Scopus indexes 49.2M+ patent records from five offices: WIPO, EPO, USPTO, JPO, UK IPO. Patents are a distinct content vertical, searchable separately from journal literature. Violation: agent misstates which offices are covered; agent gives wrong guidance on patent search availability.

PA13.label: Author identity and profile management
PA13.description: Scopus assigns a unique Author Identifier using algorithmic matching; 17.6M+ profiles; ORCID synced monthly. Profile corrections via Author Feedback Wizard within 5 working days. Violation: agent misstates correction timeline; agent claims merge/demerge is impossible; agent gives wrong Author Feedback Wizard guidance.

PA14.label: Affiliation profile curation
PA14.description: Scopus maintains 94,800+ affiliation profiles using algorithmic processing and a curated organisation database. Authorized representatives can request corrections via Institution Profile Wizard. Violation: agent claims corrections cannot be made; agent directs customer to wrong process; agent misstates the responsible team.

PA15.label: Open Access classification
PA15.description: Scopus classifies articles via Unpaywall: Gold (fully OA journal), Hybrid Gold (OA in subscription journal), Bronze (free on publisher site without explicit licence), Green (accepted manuscript in repository). Applies at document and journal level. Violation: agent confuses OA categories; agent claims OA status cannot be corrected; agent misstates how classification is determined.

PA16.label: Errata and record corrections
PA16.description: Erratum notices are indexed as a distinct document type and linked bidirectionally to the original article. Bibliographic metadata corrections follow the errata capture workflow. Violation: agent claims corrections cannot be processed; agent misstates the processing timeline; agent fails to explain the bidirectional link between erratum and original. A data correction request is processed only when Scopus content differs from the original publisher PDF/source. If Scopus already matches the publisher-supplied PDF, the correction is rejected: the error is between the author and publisher, not in Scopus metadata.

PA17.label: Cited references coverage and linkage
PA17.description: Scopus indexes cited references for documents from 1970 onward (expanded from 1996 in 2014); pre-1996 data sourced from 60 major publisher archives. References are linked when the cited source is itself indexed; unlinked references appear as plain text. Violation: agent misstates the cutoff year; agent claims older references should be linked when outside coverage; agent fails to explain why some references are not clickable.

PA18.label: Missing content processing eligibility
PA18.description: A missing content report is eligible for investigation only when all six criteria are met: (1) the source journal is selected in Scopus; (2) the journal is actively indexed (including ceased and newly-accepted titles); (3) the article publication date falls within the journal Scopus coverage period; (4) the article can be found at the publisher authentic online sourcing URL (print and electronic PDFs excluded); (5) the article was published at least 6 weeks before the support request is raised -- content published more recently will not be processed; (6) the document type is Gen-CAR (a Scopus-covered type -- excludes obituaries, reprints, etc.). AiP records bypass criteria 4-5 and follow the PA10 4-day SLA path. Preprints follow PA9 rules. Violation: agent promises to investigate content published less than 6 weeks ago; agent does not verify authentic sourcing URL before escalating; agent quotes a timeline without first checking journal indexing status.

PC2.description: The Scopus content policy area that governs the ticket topic.

PC3.label: Customer root cause

PU2.1.label: Confusing policy wording
PU2.1.description: The policy language is unclear, technical, or ambiguous -- customer confusion is a natural consequence of the wording itself

PU2.2.label: Lack of policy awareness
PU2.2.description: Customer was simply unaware the policy existed before contacting support

PU2.3.label: Agent explanation issue
PU2.3.description: Customer understood the policy when it was properly explained -- confusion arose from an unclear or incomplete agent explanation

PU2.4.label: Policy disagreement
PU2.4.description: Customer understands the policy but disputes whether it should apply to their case

PU2.5.label: Not applicable -- no customer understanding issue

PC3.description: Why the customer demonstrated difficulty understanding or accepting the applicable policy
